{{Short description|American mathematician}}
'''James "Jim" Barker Coykendall IV''' is an American mathematician.

== Education and Career ==
Coykendall was born in 1967. Coykendall earned his bachelor's degree from the [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1989 and completed a doctorate at [[Cornell University]] in 1995.<ref name="clemsonprofile">{{cite news |title=Jim Coykendall Mathematical and Statistical Sciences |url=https://www.clemson.edu/science/departments/math-stat/directory/profiles/jcoyken |access-date=4 April 2022 |publisher=Clemson University}}</ref><ref name="clemsonideas" /> His thesis, titled ''Normsets and Rings of Algebraic Integers'', was overseen by [[Shankar Sen]].<ref>{{cite thesis |type=PhD |last=Coykendall |first=James Barker |date=1995 |title=Normsets and rings of algebraic integers |publisher=Cornell University |id={{ProQuest|9528210}}}}</ref><ref>{{MathGenealogy}}</ref> After earning his doctorate, Coykendall was the C. C. Hsiung Visiting Professor of Mathematics at [[Lehigh University]] until 1996. Coykendall's teaching career continued at [[North Dakota State University]], where he was named James A. Meier Professor in 2003.<ref>{{cite news |title=Jim Coykendall Professor of Mathematics/James A. Meier Professor |url=https://www.ndsu.edu/pubweb/~coykenda/ |access-date=4 April 2022 |publisher=North Dakota State University}}</ref><ref name="clemsonideas">{{cite news |title=News from around the college: leadership changes |url=https://www.clemson.edu/cecas/files/pdfs/ideas/ideas-fall13.pdf |access-date=4 April 2022 |work=Ideas |publisher=Clemson University |date=2013}}</ref> Coykendall joined the faculty of [[Clemson University]] in 2013 and served as the Department Chair of the Mathematical Sciences Department from 2013 to 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://profiles.musc.edu/display/3269961/|title=James Coykendall|publisher=Palmetto Profiles|access-date=13 October 2024}}</ref>

Coykendall and [[Hal Schenck]] have served as editors of the ''[[Journal of Commutative Algebra]]'' since the publication's first issue in 2009.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Coykendall |first1=Jim |last2=Schenck |first2=Hal |author2-link=Hal Schenck |title=Preface |journal= Journal of Commutative Algebra|date=2009 |volume=1 |issue=1 |pages=1–2 |doi=10.1216/JCA-2009-1-1-1}}</ref> Coykendall also serves on the editorial boards of the ''Rocky Mountain Journal of Mathematics'' and the ''International Journal of Commutative Rings''.<ref>{{cite news |title=Jim Coykendall Professor of Mathematics/James A. Meier Professor |url=https://www.ndsu.edu/pubweb/~coykenda/ |access-date=4 April 2022 |publisher=North Dakota State University}}{{cite news |title=News from around the college: leadership changes |url=https://www.clemson.edu/cecas/files/pdfs/ideas/ideas-fall13.pdf |access-date=4 April 2022 |work=Ideas |publisher=Clemson University |date=2013}}</ref>

Coykendall has made significant contributions to research in commutative algebra, particularly in the study of factorization properties of rings and ideals. He presented his work on ''Normsets and Factorization Properties of Rings of Integers'' at the 1996 Spring Southeastern Sectional Meeting of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in Baton Rouge.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ams.org/meetings/sectional/1996_spring_southeastern |title=AMS :: 1996 Spring Southeastern Sectional Meeting, Program by Special Session |publisher=American Mathematical Society |access-date=13 October 2024}}</ref> His research has been widely published, and he has co-authored articles such as ''Sets with Few Intersection Numbers from Singer Subgroup Orbits'', which appeared in the ''European Journal of Combinatorics''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dblp.org/rec/journals/ejc/CoykendallD01 |title=Sets with Few Intersection Numbers from Singer Subgroup Orbits |publisher=dblp |access-date=13 October 2024}}</ref>

According to the [[Mathematics Genealogy Project]], Coykendall has supervised 17 doctoral students, as of January 2026.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=46559|title=James Coykendall IV - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|publisher=Mathematics Genealogy Project|access-date=29 Jan 2026}}</ref>
